You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
node.criteria: Compose the explicit evidence about the same original target, not the number of passes. Return complete when an established counterpart of the source DVD is white and remains identifiable as a DVD. Do not combine whiteness of one edited object with DVD identity of another. Return partial when comparison establishes requested whitening and completion is demonstrably unmet, such as an intermediate nonwhite surface or an established white transformation with loss of DVD identity. Return absent when explicit comparison evidence establishes no requested color progress on the original target; uncertain identity need not block this outcome. A failed white-endpoint check alone does not distinguish partial from absent. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations establish neither failure nor success. If correspondence or another necessary fact leaves completion versus noncompletion genuinely uncertain, return unknown unless explicit evidence independently establishes partial or absent. Unrelated additions, target disappearance, and changed shape alone do not establish requested progress or its absence. Preserve uncertainty and do not use the reference label as evidence.
node.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: Both supplied checks report that the source DVD’s correspondence to either edited white disc is indeterminate. Without establishing which edited object is the original DVD, its whitening and retained DVD identity cannot be determined.

dependencies.evidence: The central printed rectangular item in the source is replaced by a white disc in the edit, while the separate object farther right also appears as a white disc. The changed shape and shared position do not establish which edited disc corresponds to the specified black DVD, so the requested DVD’s color cannot be determined confidently.

The source target is the small rectangular printed item near the center, but the edited image shows two white discs: a solid oval near the center and a separate disc with a visible opening on the right. The source-to-edit correspondence is indeterminate, so neither edited disc can be confidently identified as the requested DVD.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is internally inconsistent: it describes the target as already visibly white, while the instruction and reference identify the black DVD in the source. Bind explicitly to that source object and preserve its identity across the edit; do not treat either white edited disc as the target merely because it is white or nearby. The traces show a small printed rectangular item at center in the source and two white discs in the edit, so correspondence is genuinely ambiguous from these images; changed shape and position alone do not resolve it. Improve the node’s evidence criteria to compare distinctive location/appearance and DVD cues across images, and to return unknown when correspondence remains unresolved. If evidence independently establishes no color progress on the original target, allow absent without requiring DVD identity in the edit; do not infer absent from a failed endpoint check or use the reference label as evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported."}
